## Code Review

This pull request adds support for Huawei NPUs (Ascend) to the Verl framework, specifically for sglang with FSDP. The changes include adding NPU-specific environment variables, abstracting device-dependent code in the sglang rollout worker, and modifying the FSDP sharding manager for NPU compatibility. A new example script for running on NPUs is also included.

My review identifies two high-severity issues. First, the new example script contains hardcoded, user-specific paths, which hinders portability and usability. It's recommended to parameterize these paths. Second, the FSDP sharding manager introduces a module-level global flag for one-time PID registration, which is not robust. This should be refactored into an instance variable to avoid potential bugs in complex scenarios.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

This script contains several hardcoded absolute paths which are specific to a user's environment (lines 2, 12, 26, 27, 33). This makes the script not portable and difficult for others to use. It's highly recommended to replace these with variables defined at the top of the script, which users can easily configure. This would make the example script much more reusable.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Using a module-level global variable `set_pid_flag` is not a robust pattern for controlling one-time initialization within a class instance. It can lead to bugs if multiple `FSDPSGLangShardingManager` instances are created. Please remove this global flag and use an instance variable instead, initialized in the `__init__` method (e.g., `self._pids_registered = False`).

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

This block should use an instance variable for one-time execution control, to fix the issue with the global `set_pid_flag`. Additionally, the `print()` statement on line 124 should be replaced with a `logger` call for proper logging.

Assuming `self._pids_registered` is initialized to `False` in `__init__`, this block should be refactored as follows:

```suggestion
        if not self._pids_registered:
            if self.device_mesh["infer_tp"].get_local_rank() != 0:
                tp_size = self.device_mesh["infer_tp"].size()
                result_pid = torch.zeros(tp_size, dtype=torch.int64)
                result_pid = result_pid.to("npu")
            else:
                result_pid = self.inference_engine.result_pid
                result_pid = torch.tensor(result_pid, dtype=torch.int64, device="npu")

            dist.broadcast(result_pid, src=self.device_mesh["infer_tp"].mesh.tolist()[0], group=self.device_mesh["infer_tp"].get_group(),)
            for pid in result_pid:
                torch_npu._C._add_ipc_pid(pid)

            logger.info(f"the pids from sglang is {result_pid}")
            self._pids_registered = True
```

reviews.body:
## Code Review

This pull request adds support for Huawei NPUs (Ascend) to the Verl framework, specifically for sglang with FSDP. The changes include adding NPU-specific environment variables, abstracting device-dependent code in the sglang rollout worker, and modifying the FSDP sharding manager for NPU compatibility. A new example script for running on NPUs is also included.

My review identifies two high-severity issues. First, the new example script contains hardcoded, user-specific paths, which hinders portability and usability. It's recommended to parameterize these paths. Second, the FSDP sharding manager introduces a module-level global flag for one-time PID registration, which is not robust. This should be refactored into an instance variable to avoid potential bugs in complex scenarios.
